artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan fixing the CLAUDE.md double-body via computed-artifact regeneration in sync.lua and the duplicate Stop-hook via a matcher-aware, self-normalizing settings merge in merge.lua
Orchestrator handoff recording planned status, 6 phases, and the 4-wave dependency structure

memory_candidates.content: In the nvim extension-loader deploy system, merge targets fall into two structurally different regimes that must not be mixed. Computed artifacts (claudemd/opencode_md merge keys, opencode.json) are regenerated wholesale by generate_claudemd()/generate_opencode_json() and deliberately carry NO section markers; incremental-append targets (settings, index) are merged in place and never regenerated. When a defect shows duplicated content in a computed artifact, the cause is almost always a caller still driving the retired incremental primitive (inject_section) against a file the computed regime owns -- check every caller for regime agreement rather than restoring markers. A computed artifact self-heals on the next regeneration, which makes the defect intermittent and makes a clean live file worthless as evidence of absence; an incremental-append target does not self-heal and its duplicates are a one-way ratchet.
